title: Replacing Gas Hot Water with a Heat Pump: What to Check First
seoTitle: Replacing Gas Hot Water with a Heat Pump: What to Check First
description: Thinking of replacing an old gas hot water system with a heat pump? Learn what Australian homeowners should review before upgrading.
excerpt: If your old gas hot water system is becoming unreliable, slow to recover, expensive to run, or close to the end of its life, you may be considering whether to replace it…
html:
If your old gas hot water system is becoming unreliable, slow to recover, expensive to run, or close to the end of its life, you may be considering whether to replace it with another gas unit or move to a heat pump hot water system.

For many Australian homeowners, this decision is no longer just about replacing like-for-like. It is also about energy use, property suitability, household hot water demand, installation conditions, state-based eligibility, and long-term plans for the home.

If your current gas hot water system is ageing or no longer meeting your household needs, Auzbright can help you check your eligibility and explore heat pump hot water upgrade options before you make a decision.

Direct Answer: Should you replace gas hot water with a heat pump?

Replacing an old gas hot water system with a heat pump may make sense if your current system is inefficient, unreliable, expensive to operate, or no longer suits your household. Before upgrading, homeowners should check property suitability, installation space, hot water demand, existing gas setup, electrical requirements, eligibility, quote inclusions and long-term usage. A heat pump is not automatically the right choice for every home, so a proper assessment is important.

1. Start with the condition of your current gas system

Before deciding on a replacement, look at how your current gas hot water system is performing. Some systems fail suddenly, while others show warning signs over time.

Common signs to review include:

  • inconsistent hot water
  • long recovery time
  • frequent repairs
  • rising gas bills
  • unusual noises
  • pilot light or ignition issues
  • visible rust or leaks
  • the system no longer meeting household demand
  • age of the system

If the system is still working but clearly ageing, you may have more time to compare options properly. If it fails suddenly, many homeowners rush into the quickest replacement. Auzbright can help you review whether a heat pump option may be suitable before you simply replace gas with gas again.

2. Understand how a heat pump is different from gas hot water

A gas hot water system uses gas to heat water, either in a storage tank or on demand. A heat pump system uses electricity to operate a refrigeration-style cycle that draws heat from the surrounding air and transfers it to the water.

This difference matters because the home’s setup may need review. A heat pump may suit some properties well, while others may need extra checks around location, electrical connection, drainage, noise and access.

A heat pump is not just a different brand of hot water system. It is a different type of technology, so the upgrade should be planned properly.

Also note the age, condition, reliability and service history. If repairs are becoming more frequent or the system is no longer keeping up, it may be time to review upgrade options before a sudden failure forces a rushed decision.

3. Check whether your property has suitable installation space

Heat pump hot water systems usually need suitable space, airflow and access. Some gas systems are installed in areas that may not be suitable for a heat pump without changes.

Before replacing your old gas hot water system, check:

FactorWhy It Matters
Outdoor spaceHeat pumps often need a suitable location with airflow.
Drainageondensate and plumbing requirements may need review.
Electrical accessElectrical suitability may need to be checked.
Noise locationPlacement should consider bedrooms, neighbours and living areas.
Installer accessSafe access is needed for installation and future servicing.
Existing gas locationThe old gas unit position may not always suit the new heat pump.

A site-specific review is important because two homes with similar hot water systems can still need different installation solutions.

4. Review household hot water usage

Your household usage should guide the system choice. A couple in a small home may have different hot water needs from a family with multiple bathrooms and heavy morning demand.

Before requesting a quote, think about:

  • How many people live in the home?
  • How many bathrooms are used regularly?
  • When is hot water demand highest?
  • Does the current gas system keep up?
  • Do you often run out of hot water?
  • Do you use hot water heavily for laundry or cleaning?
  • Are your household needs likely to change?

The heat pump should be matched to real usage rather than selected only by price or product name.

5. Check electrical and gas disconnection considerations

Replacing gas hot water with a heat pump may involve more than removing one unit and installing another. Depending on the property, the installer may need to review electrical requirements, plumbing changes, old system removal, and what happens to the existing gas connection.

Homeowners should ask:

  • Will electrical work be required?
  • Is the switchboard suitable?
  • What happens to the old gas unit?
  • Is gas disconnection included or separate?
  • Are plumbing changes needed?
  • Are there any extra site costs?
  • What certificates or paperwork are provided?

These details should be clear before approving the upgrade.

6. Understand eligibility by state

Energy-efficiency support can vary depending on where your property is located. Victorian households may need to check Victorian Energy Upgrades requirements where relevant. NSW households may need to check NSW energy-saving pathways where applicable. Other Australian states may have different rules or different availability.

Do not assume that a claim you see in one state applies in another. Also avoid relying on broad statements such as “everyone qualifies” or “free upgrade for all homes”. Eligibility can depend on the property, existing system, product selection, installation conditions and current program rules.

Auzbright can help homeowners check which pathway may apply before relying on a rebate or discount claim.

7. Compare the full quote, not just the upgrade offer

A heat pump quote should explain what is included and what may cost extra. Before booking, check whether the quote includes:

  • supply of the heat pump hot water system
  • standard installation
  • removal of the old gas system if required
  • plumbing work
  • electrical work
  • gas disconnection or related work if applicable
  • eligibility assessment
  • paperwork and certificates
  • any exclusions or site-specific extras

A low starting point can be useful, but the final decision should be based on the actual quote for your property.

8. Be careful with savings claims

A heat pump hot water system may help reduce hot water energy use compared with some older systems, but savings are not the same for every home. Usage habits, tariffs, system type, installation quality, weather, maintenance and household demand all affect the outcome.

A responsible provider should not promise the same saving for every household. Instead, they should review your current system, property and usage before explaining what may be suitable.

FAQs

Can I replace a gas hot water system with a heat pump?

Yes, many homeowners may be able to consider replacing an old gas hot water system with a heat pump. Suitability depends on property layout, installation space, electrical requirements, household demand and current eligibility rules.

Is a heat pump better than gas hot water?

It depends on your home and usage. A heat pump may be more energy-efficient than some older systems, but the right choice depends on installation conditions, household needs, tariffs, product suitability and available support.

Will I need electrical work when replacing gas hot water with a heat pump?

Some homes may need electrical checks or electrical work before installation. This depends on the existing setup, switchboard, system type and installation requirements.

Can I get a rebate for replacing gas hot water with a heat pump?

Eligible households may be able to access support through relevant state-based energy-efficiency pathways. Eligibility can vary, so homeowners should check their situation with Auzbright before relying on any rebate claim.

Should I wait until my gas hot water system fails?

Not always. If your system is old, unreliable or no longer suitable, reviewing options before it fails can give you more time to compare suitable systems, check eligibility and avoid a rushed decision.
